https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cvgy.text: Image source, NurPhoto via Getty Images Image caption, Protesters hold a banner showing the face of the child who was killed By Phanindra Dahal Â and Â Azadeh Moshiri Published 7 hours ago Activists and politicians in Nepal have urged the government to enact tougher laws as the alleged rape and murder of a three-year-old girl has caused outrage across the country. Nepal has seen continued protests since the girl was found dead last week, three days after she went missing in Madhesh province. Nine people have been arrested in connection with the case, a local police spokesman told the BBC. The crime has triggered demands for reform. Police have also been accused of negligence in the initial stages of the investigation after footage of a teenage suspect was leaked onto social media. After days of demonstrations in the city of Simara, the victim's family met government ministers, and secured a written agreement over the weekend. The government has promised to review laws on serious offences, and create a memorial in honour of the child. The incident has also opened a wider debate over how Nepal deals with young offenders, with some campaigners pushing for harsher punishments for minors convicted of rape or murder. Prominent human rights activist Gauri Pradhan called the attack a "very painful incident and the government should punish anyone involved in such atrocious act. There should be some serious efforts for wider reforms". However, he cautioned against calls for the introduction of the death penalty. There has also been anger after a video showing a teenage suspect giving a statement about the suspected murder was uploaded to social media, sparking questions as to how footage of the individual under police custody was leaked. "We have so far found one police personnel directly involved in the [leak] and have initiated action against him," chief district officer of Bara district, Dharmendra Kumar Mishra, told the BBC. "If more officers are found, they will also be punished. We have zero tolerance against such practice." More than 25,500 accusations of rape and sexual abuse were filed between July 2017 to July 2025, according to Nepalese Police. Of these cases, more than 3,200 female victims were under the age of 10, the police say. Az Európai Unió Tanácsa kedden közölte , hogy további 36 hónapra fenntartja a szankciókat azok ellen, akiket felelősnek tekint Ukrajna területi egységének, önrendelkezésének és függetlenségének aláaknázásáért. A tagállami kormányokat képviselő uniós testület hozzátette: összesen több mint 3000 személyt és céget, szervezetet sújtottak beutazási tilalommal és vagyonbefagyasztással. A Tanács a közleménye szerint úgy döntött, hogy nem újítja meg három személy és egy cég vagy szervezet listázását, valakit pedig azért húztak le, mert időközben elhunyt. Hivatalosan még nem frissítették a listát , de több lap – köztük öt forrásra hivatkozva a Politico – arról írt, hogy levettek róla két oligarchát, Aliser Uszmanovot és Mihail Fridmant. Az EUobserver márciusban arról írt , hogy a szlovák kormány Uszmanovot és Fridmant is megpróbálta kihúzatni, az akkori magyar vezetés pedig – öt másik név mellett – szóban támogatta a próbálkozást, de végül nem csatlakozott a vétókísérlethez, az elszigetelt szlovákok pedig ejtették az ügyet. Most a Politico szerint Uszmanovot a francia, a befagyasztott vagyona miatt Luxemburgot perelő Fridmant a luxemburgi kormány is támogatta, míg a másik oldalon balti és északi országok sorakoztak fel. Utóbbiaknak tehettek engedményt azzal, hogy a szokásos fél év helyett háromra hosszabbították meg a szankciókat. A Financial Times nemrég arról írt, hogy a francia kormány Azerbajdzsánban bebörtönzött franciák elengedéséért cserébe szedhette le Uszmanovot. https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/uk-.text: A warning has been issued to people with plans to travel to Belgium. The European country is a popular travel destination with millions heading there from the UK each year. The Foreign Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) regularly keeps UK holidaymakers updated with the latest guidance to ensure their trip runs smoothly. An update has been issued on the FCDO official website that anyone travelling to Belgium should be aware of strike action that could impact their visit. The guidance said: "A large-scale demonstration is expected to take place in central Brussels on Friday 9 October. There is no confirmation on whether this will affect public transport or wider public services including schools. "A public sector strike is planned on Monday 12 October. This may affect public transport and other public services. General strikes took place on 31 March, 29 April, 14 October, 26 November, 15 December 2025 and 12 March and 12 May 2026. Strike action may be announced at short notice. "Monitor local news and check with your provider regarding potential delays and closures. Always check with your travel operator for the latest updates." Trade union ACOD/VGSP are planning a protest in Belgium on this date to demonstrate against a round of budget cuts. There are no direct flights from Liverpool John Lennon Airport to Belgium. However, it is a popular route from nearby Manchester Airport, which offers direct flights that take around one hour and 25 minutes. It has been a busy week for the Speke -based airport as Ryanair announced new flight routes from Liverpool. The budget airline has unveiled a big expansion of its winter schedule. Starting this winter, Ryanair will fly from Liverpool to Milan Bergamo, Copenhagen, Gdańsk, Porto, Tirana, and Warsaw. While most of those destinations are colder cities where festive activities will be at the top of the itinerary, Porto can offer a slice of sunshine during the winter months. The change softens the timeline after Ireland, which holds the rotating presidency of the Council of the EU, said that it aims to open the two remaining clusters – Cluster 4, on the green agenda and sustainable connectivity, and Cluster 5, on resources, agriculture and cohesion – before the end of the year. by Kyiv Post | Oct. 15, 2026, 7:02 pm Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied European flags flutter outside the Berlaymont building of the EU Commission headquarters in Brussels on Oct. 2, 2026. (Photo by Nicolas TUCAT / AFP) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip The EU officials have removed the phrase “as soon as possible” from their draft conclusion for the Oct. 15-16 European Council summit regarding the opening of the remaining accession clusters for Ukraine and Moldova. The change was reported Thursday by European Pravda , whose correspondent compared versions of the draft dated Oct. 13 and Oct. 14. in Brussels. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . Accession negotiations cover 33 chapters grouped into six clusters that organize the legal and institutional reforms Ukraine must adopt and implement in order to formally join the EU. So far, Ukraine and Moldova opened Cluster 1 – Fundamentals on June 15, and Cluster 6 – External Relations on July 14. Clusters 2 and 3 were opened on Tuesday, Oct. 13. after Hungary lifted its long-standing veto on Ukraine’s accession bid. Advertisement The two countries’ paths remain closely linked, and any decision regarding their accession requires unanimous support from all 27 states. What changed The softer wording comes as Ireland, which holds the rotating presidency of the Council of the EU, said it aims to open Ukraine’s two remaining clusters – Cluster 4, on the green agenda and sustainable connectivity, and Cluster 5, on resources, agriculture and cohesion – before the end of 2026. In the Oct. 13 version, the section on Ukraine said EU leaders looked forward to opening all other clusters as soon as possible, in line with the bloc’s merit-based approach. Other Topics of Interest Zelensky Outlines 3 Security Options as US Pushes for November Talks With Russia Zelensky details NATO, US and European security options, rejects limits on Ukraine’s army and says Putin agreed to November talks. The updated draft keeps the expectation that the clusters will be opened under the merit-based approach but no longer includes any reference to timing. The same edit was made to a separate paragraph on Moldova, which also previously called for the remaining clusters to be opened as soon as possible. Clusters opened after months of stagnation According to European Pravda, both paragraphs still welcome the intergovernmental conferences held on Tuesday, Oct. 13, at which Clusters 2 and 3 were opened for Ukraine and Moldova , following months of stagnation due to Hungary’s veto. Advertisement The breakthrough finally came through after Ukraine’s parliament, the Verkhovna Rada, passed amendments expanding education rights for national minorities and introduced a special status for general secondary schools serving national minorities. Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar welcomed the move in a statement , saying that the amendments would make it fundamentally easier for Hungarian children in Ukraine’s Transcarpathia region to use their native language. Hours after Ukraine adopted the law, Hungary dropped its long-standing veto and made it possible for the country to continue its path towards the EU. “I can confirm that all EU member states have agreed to: open clusters 2 and 3 for Ukraine and Moldova,” Irish Minister of State for European Affairs and Defence Thomas Byrne said on Monday, Oct. 12, calling Oct. 13 another “Super Tuesday” for the candidate countries. The European Commission previously proposed limiting Ukraine’s access to EU farm subsidies and markets for sensitive products even after accession , which Agriculture Minister Taras Vysotskyi rejected on Tuesday, Oct. 5. by saying that Kyiv cannot accept permanent restrictions. Advertisement Hungary’s long-standing veto Ukraine’s application had been largely stalled for years due to vetoes from Hungary ’s former-leader Viktor Orbán. His defeat by Magyar in April removed the blockage, allowing talks to resume. However, Magyar’s diplomatic stance on Ukraine continues to repeatedly shift, and Ukrainian authorities have linked it to that of Orbán for several times. In June, President Volodymyr Zelensky and Magyar sealed what the Hungarian PM described as a “ historic agreement ,” formally securing the political, educational, cultural and linguistic rights of ethnic Hungarian communities in Transcarpathia. Budapest later tied the opening of further clusters to Ukraine turning those commitments into law. Around the same time in June, Magyar said he secured the removal of language accelerating Ukraine’s EU accession from the European Council summit declaration after four hours of negotiations. The conclusion welcomed Ukraine’s accession process but omitted its speeding up. By blocking the joint letter to the European Council and Commission outlining the EU’s common position on opening five remaining clusters, Hungary became the sole objector among all member states. During a Council of the EU working group meeting on July 17, Hungary blocked the procedure . Although Budapest agreed to advance Cluster 3 for Moldova, other member states rejected the request decoupling the two candidate countries. Advertisement No conclusion was reached at the time. Hungary then blocked Clusters 2 and 3 again on July 22. “There are six clusters in total, and we don’t think opening them all at once is a good idea – partly because the ink on the first one isn’t even dry yet, and partly because it would send the wrong message to the countries of the Western Balkans,” Magyar told reporters at the Council meeting in Brussels. On Sept. 8, Ukraine faced its fourth refusal from Hungary , as Kyiv said Budapest had yet to specify its demands in exchange for lifting its objection. “For 17 months, the government of Viktor Orbán blocked the opening of clusters, although Ukraine has fulfilled all the conditions for this,” Ukrainian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi told European Pravda . “But even having lost power, Orbán’s team continues to disrupt the normalization of Hungary’s relations with Ukraine,” he continued. During his tenure, Orbán repeatedly cited concerns over the rights of the Hungarian minority as a reason Hungary had delayed opening the first negotiation cluster. Hungary previously also blocked technical work on clusters 2 through 6 for Ukraine, later lifting its objection to Cluster 6, covering foreign and security policy, trade policy, and relations with third countries.
